title: Rule 7 decoder must reject noncanonical modes, directions, and residue padding
description: Security/interoperability review finding: spec/03-adaptation.md mandates canonical Rule 7 compressor choices but does not require decoders to reject alternate encodings of the same IPv6/UDP packet. AddressMode=1 with two canonical fe80::/64 addresses, PortDirection=1 with OtherPort=10883 when both ports are 10883, and nonzero octet-padding bits can be accepted and normalized by permissive decoders. This wire malleability undermines bit-exact interoperability, can create different strict/permissive trust behavior, and weakens assumptions that a decompressed packet has one canonical signed representation.
acceptance_criteria: The normative Rule 7 decoder requirements say MUST reject full-address mode when both addresses qualify for canonical fe80::/64 IID mode, MUST reject PortDirection=1 with OtherPort=10883 for the both-ports case, and MUST reject every nonzero residue padding bit. Canonical negative vectors cover each malleable form and Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python reject them identically. Positive canonical src-only, dst-only, both-port, link-local, and full-address vectors remain bit-identical.
